new: **English reference answer（笔记自拟，旧解压目录实跑口径）**: I compare OLS, Ridge, LASSO, Elastic Net, PCR and PLS under the stated weekly split, select settings on validation weeks, and refit the full preprocessing/model pipeline through June 2025 before evaluating the untouched test weeks against zero excess return. Within-family validation settings are Ridge alpha=1000, LASSO alpha=0.003, Elastic Net alpha=0.01 with l1_ratio=0.25, PCR K=5, and PLS K=1; OLS has no tuning parameter. The comparison selects PCR with five components. Test OOS $R^2$ values against zero are approximately −0.531% (OLS), −0.151% (Ridge), −0.136% (LASSO), −0.136% (Elastic Net), +0.024% (PCR), and +0.054% (PLS).

For CCB (0939.HK) in the test week 2025-07-04, the frozen PCR rule predicts an excess return of about 0.85%, while the realized excess return is about 2.16%. I read the model comparison before tracing that row; agreement between the manual and pipeline prediction checks implementation consistency, not forecast accuracy or deployability.
